title: Envelope: contract (v2)
description: A versioned contract descriptor whose explicit artifacts array defines the bounded contract-set-v2 carried set.

x_binding.description: P5 2026-08-10: what this contract IS and whether it can be adopted or pinned. Carried under the sanctioned `x_` prefix (patternProperties below) rather than as a bare `binding`, because unlike envelope/v2/work_request this schema is already deployed (a live contract carries `schema: envelope/v2`) and closes with unevaluatedProperties: false — an older binary reading a legal document must still accept it. Same value grammar as work_request's `binding`: either the literal `none`, or the four declarations. Absence is `undeclared`, distinct from a declared `none` (P-1) — this field is optional, not required.

artifact_class.description: What kind of thing this is, author's own vocabulary — e.g. non_binding_review.

compatibility_status.description: The compatibility claim being made, or "none" to make no claim at all.

adoptable.description: Whether `a2a contract adopt` may target this contract.

runtime_pinnable.description: Whether a consumer may pin a runtime dependency against it.

allOf.description: T2's asymmetry: a `compatibility_status: none` claim inside the long form must be as unadoptable and unpinnable as the bare `none` sentinel, or the long form reopens the escape hatch T2 names — the sentinel and the long form must not disagree.

x_operational.description: P5 2026-08-10, specs/05-declared-nature.md's AC1 discharge half: readiness of the operational half of the interface this contract describes, per named item -- endpoint, credential-channel, registration are the items §7 names, and a fourth kind is DATA (a new array entry), not a schema change. Carried under the sanctioned `x_` prefix for the SAME reason as `x_binding`: this schema is deployed and closes with unevaluatedProperties: false. Each entry's own PRESENCE is the author's declaration -- a named item absent from this array, or the whole field absent, reads as `undeclared` downstream (P-1), distinct from a declared `state: absent`; that reading is the CALLER's (pendency's), never this schema's, to make -- this field carries no default and absence is never `ready`. `eta` is not a clock: a declared date, so a reader can tell "next week" from "not this quarter"; the domain still reads no clock (seam.md §6).

name.description: The operational item this entry declares -- e.g. endpoint, credential-channel, registration. Free text, not a closed enum: a fourth kind is data.

eta.description: A declared date this item is expected to reach `ready` -- not a clock the system polls.

x_identity.description: P5 2026-08-28 (docs/features/active/no-silent-yes-2026-08/specs/05-a-contract-says-what-it-must.md, US-1): the producer's keying rule for the records this contract's carried set describes -- `keys` names the field(s) a consumer must key one logical record on, `dynamic_keys_from` optionally names an axis whose declared values supply additional per-value keys the fixed `keys` list cannot enumerate ahead of time, and `on_redelivery` states whether a redelivered record REPLACES the prior one under the same key (`upsert`) or is treated as a new entry (`append`). Carried under the sanctioned `x_` prefix for the SAME reason as `x_binding`/`x_operational`: this schema is deployed and closes with unevaluatedProperties: false, so an older binary reading a legal document must still accept it. This field absent reads as `undeclared` downstream, distinct from a declared value; that reading is the CALLER's, never this schema's, to make -- a consumer that assumes a keying rule where none was declared is the exact silent-duplication failure this field exists to prevent.

keys.description: The field(s) that together identify one logical record a consumer must key on.

dynamic_keys_from.description: Names an axis whose declared values supply additional per-value keys at runtime, when the key set is not fixed ahead of time.

on_redelivery.description: Whether a redelivered record replaces the prior one under the same key (upsert) or is treated as a new entry (append).

x_guarantees.description: P5 2026-08-28 (same spec, US-3): the producer's checkable promises about the records this contract describes, drawn from a closed vocabulary -- `required_non_null` (no record carries a null in a field this contract requires) and `deterministic_keys` (the same logical record always keys to the same value) to start -- rather than free-text prose an unlisted value is refused, not silently carried. An empty array is a legal, deliberate claim of no guarantees. This field absent reads as `undeclared` downstream, distinct from a declared empty value; that reading is the CALLER's, never this schema's, to make -- absence is never a promise a consumer may assume.

x_schema_location.description: P5 2026-08-28 (same spec, US-4): the repo-relative path to this contract's machine schema, so a consumer can find it without parsing a sentence -- today this is only ever stated in prose (e.g. provides/<slug>/schema/). An absolute path or a path carrying a `..` traversal segment is refused by this field's own pattern. This field absent reads as `undeclared` downstream, distinct from a declared value; that reading is the CALLER's, never this schema's, to make -- absence means the location must still be found in prose, not that no machine schema exists.
